checks.claim: C1: Z_mass and R are positive and finite for 0<a<1, D>0; all needed moments are finite; D-compact bounds hold; the normalized object is the actual joint density, not a Gaussian tilt or product law.
checks.reason: The substitution v=s lambda^2/(2D) reproduces (5) exactly, including the factor 1/2 and exponent (a+j)/2. The s-integrability exponents are -a/2, (1-a)/2 and -a/2 for (j,ell)=(0,0),(1,1),(2,1), all >-1. Dropping e^(-s lambda)<=1 and using exp(-s lambda^2/(2D))<=exp(-s lambda^2/(2D_+)) gives the compact-D domination. Positivity holds because the integrand is positive on an open rectangle. Lines 83-85 define the normalized law from the actual density and assert no product structure. The E_D[s] factor used in Cauchy-Schwarz is trivially bounded (see minor note).

checks.claim: C2: Fixed-s>0 lambda-IBP, both endpoints, separate joint integrability of the three terms, Fubini and null s=0 give m1+m2=a; Cauchy-Schwarz gives m1^2<=D m2/2; moment_lower applies with exact guards to give (8).
checks.reason: The derivative of lambda^a exp[-s(lambda+lambda^2/(2D))] is exactly the three stated terms. The endpoint at 0 vanishes since a>0, and the endpoint at infinity vanishes by Gaussian decay for fixed s>0. The terms correspond to (j,ell)=(0,0),(1,1),(2,1), each with finite joint absolute integral. Dividing by Z_mass gives a-m1-m2=0, with m2=E_D[s lambda^2]/D. Cauchy-Schwarz with sqrt(s), sqrt(s)lambda and E_D[s]<=1/2 gives m1^2<=(1/2)E_D[s lambda^2]=D m2/2; the half and the D are retained. The pp.all type of moment_lower has hypotheses 0<a, 0<D, x+y=a, x^2<=D*y/2 and conclusion 2*a^2/(D+4*a)<=y. Substituting x=m1, y=m2 matches. By hand, a^2-2ay<=(a-y)^2<=Dy/2 confirms the implication.

checks.claim: C3: Differentiation under the integral on compact D, partial_D log R=m2/(2D), the entropy derivative, the log1p bound, the chain rule, rational_gap and MVT monotonicity on all q>2a.
checks.reason: The D-derivative of exp(-s lambda^2/(2D)) is s lambda^2/(2D^2) times itself. The dominating function D_-^(-2)/2 * s lambda^(a+1) exp(-s lambda^2/(2D_+)) is the (2,1) case of (5). Z is differentiated as an integral, so no expectation is held fixed: Z'/Z=E_D[s lambda^2]/(2D^2)=m2/(2D). Direct calculus gives partial_q Delta=(1/2)log[q(q-2a)/(q-a)^2]; the identity (q-a)^2=qD+a^2 with q=D+2a gives (10). All log arguments q, D, q-a are positive for q>2a. dD/dq=1 and log(1+z)<=z give the lower bound. The difference equals a^2/[2(D+4a)(D+2a)] by hand and matches the rational_gap pp.all type at a,D>0. J is positive and C1 with a strictly positive derivative lower bound on the connected set (2a,infinity), so MVT gives strict monotonicity.
